study type: Observational study on human fecal microbiomes combined with an experimental Fecal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) study in germ-free mice.
exposure: Fecal microbiome from children of mothers with IBD vs. controls (for FMT)
outcome: Intestinal barrier function (Zo1, Ocln gene expression in mice)
Metabolic changes (Ido1 expression, serum kynurenine/tryptophan ratios in mice)
cohort: The study included 44 children (0-10 years old) born to 26 mothers with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) and 44 age-matched control children born to 29 mothers without IBD.
finding: Fecal microbiomes of children born to mothers with IBD exhibit characteristics, particularly from age 4, that reduce epithelial tight junction barrier genes (Zo1 and Ocln) and tolerogenic tryptophan metabolism (Ido1, kynurenine/tryptophan ratios) and cause mesenteric lymph node enlargement when transplanted to germ-free mice, suggesting a mechanism for enhanced IBD predisposition.
